title: John Henry Newman (1801–1890)
hookLine: an Oxford Anglican priest becomes Catholic, and the Church later names him a saint

cards: A sailing ship, stuck. No wind. The sea is flat, and the boat goes nowhere.

On board is a young English clergyman who has nearly died of a fever in Sicily. He badly wants to be home; he believes there is work waiting for him there, though he cannot see what it is. So he writes a short poem.
It begins with three words, and asks for very little: not a map, not the whole road, just enough light for the next step. People still sing it as a hymn.

teach.b: The clergyman was John Henry Newman. First, Oxford. Newman was a priest of the Church of England, a fellow of an Oxford college and a preacher at the university church, and his sermons drew students in.
He and his friends set out to recover the Church of England's roots in the early Church, and he read the early Christian writers closely. Second, the turn.
The deeper he read, the more convinced he became that the Catholic Church was the Church of those early writers. He was received into it.
It cost him his post, his place at Oxford and many old friendships, and he wrote that it felt like coming into port after a rough sea.
Third, the poem from the ship, written years before his conversion: "Lead, Kindly Light, amid the encircling gloom, Lead Thou me on! The night is dark, and I am far from home; Lead Thou me on!"
And the line people remember: "Keep Thou my feet; I do not ask to see The distant scene; one step enough for me." Fourth, the saint.

teach.h: A PRIEST, A CARDINAL, A SAINT.
teach.b: Newman spent his Catholic years as a priest of the Oratory in Birmingham, writing, teaching and looking after a parish, and late in life the pope made him a cardinal.
The Church has since canonized him. Anglicans honor him too, and both still sing his poem. The man who asked for one step got a long road, one step at a time.

how: Catholics keep Saint John Henry Newman's feast on October 9, and his poem Lead, Kindly Light is sung as a hymn in Catholic and Anglican churches and at funerals.

games.q: you are a respected Oxford preacher, and your reading of the early Church leads you toward the Catholic Church. what do you do?
o: stay quiet and keep your post.
become Catholic, knowing it will cost your place and friends.
games.why: Newman was received into the Catholic Church. it cost him his post at Oxford and many friendships.

practice: Think of one thing in your life where you can't see the distant scene, a decision, a worry, a road with no map, and don't try to solve it; ask only for the next step.
If you pray, say Newman's words slowly: lead, kindly light, lead thou me on. If you don't, just hold the phrase one step enough.

wordCard.voice: Oratory. The community in Birmingham where John Henry Newman spent his Catholic years as a priest, writing, teaching, and looking after a parish.

carryVoice: Your line: lead, kindly light. Looking back: a tax collector in the light, Guaraní towns, the passion, a Church renewing, the confessional, circles of givers, and one step at a time. Rest well.
